newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A decision is expected soon on the turnkey contract for a multi-million dollar downstream petrochemical project planned for Abu Dhabi with three major U.S.-based companies in the running.
- Bahrain's ministry of commerce is going ahead with changes to the commercial agency law aimed at opening up the market and indications are that they will be endorsed before the end of the year.
- Doha and Seoul finalised a deal to double gas exports to Korea to 4.8 million tonnes by the turn of the century.
- The UAE's cabinet has approved a draft amendment to a law to increase the federal tax on tobacco imports and related products to 70 percent from a current 50 percent.
- Iran is to release 20 million sturgeon fry into the Caspian Sea this year in a bid to boost its sinking caviar production, newspapers said.
- Saudi Arabia is expected to spend nearly $30 billion on new petrochemical projects by 2000, the Gulf Organisation for Industrial Consulting said.
- Saudi Arabia said it would not attend a controversial Arab-Israeli economic conference and urged Qatar to call off the event.
- Advertising expenditure in the United Arab Emirates in the first four months of the year reached $67.7 million, making it the biggest Gulf advertising market after Saudi Arabia.
